verdict.description: What you would actually do with this application after reading it: interview them, put it on the maybe pile, or pass.

first_impression.description: What you notice in the first twenty seconds, in one or two sentences. The reader is the applicant, so say it to them plainly.

strengths.description: What is working, as things you would say out loud to a hiring manager. Two to four.

concerns.description: What would make you hesitate, each with the change that would fix it. Ordered by how much it costs them.

concern.description: What a screener would hesitate over.

fix.description: The specific change to the document. Not general advice.

keywords_to_work_in.description: Terms the advertisement uses that this document does not, and that a record genuinely supports. Leave empty rather than reaching.

term.description: The advertisement's own wording for it.

supported_by.description: The id of the evidence record that shows they did this work. Must be a real id from the list you were given.

where.description: Which part of the document it belongs in, and what it would replace.

records_to_add.description: Evidence records that would strengthen this application for THIS advertisement and are not used in the document yet. Leave empty if the document already draws on the right ones.

record_id.description: A real id from the records you were given.

why.description: What this record answers in the advertisement that the document currently does not.
